claims.explanation: Monastrol selectively kills cells that depend on KIF11/Eg5-driven spindle bipolarity and have an intact spindle assembly checkpoint, so sensitivity is driven by high KIF11 expression and functional mitotic checkpoint signaling, while resistance arises from checkpoint loss or mitotic slippage. TP53 and RB1 pathway inactivation, common in the least-affected lines, permits mitotic slippage and survival after monopolar arrest, whereas sensitive lines retain TP53/RB1 and arrest/die in mitosis. Additional modifiers include PTEN/PI3K and KRAS/MAPK pathway activity that influence mitotic entry and drug response.

features.basis: monastrol directly inhibits Eg5/KIF11, so higher target expression increases dependence
TP53 loss permits mitotic slippage and survival after monopolar arrest; TP53 mutations enriched in least-affected lines
RB1 loss allows bypass of mitotic arrest/slippage; RB1 mutations enriched in resistant lines
PTEN loss/PI3K activation associated with resistance in listed lines
KRAS mutations enriched in least-affected lines, possibly via MAPK-driven mitotic adaptation
BRAF mutations appear in several resistant lines and may reduce mitotic dependence
CDKN2A loss in sensitive lines may increase mitotic entry and KIF11 dependence
ATM mutations appear in resistant lines, possibly altering checkpoint/apoptotic response
SMARCA4 mutations enriched in resistant lines, chromatin remodeling may affect mitotic gene expression
ARID1A mutations appear in resistant lines, possibly via chromatin-mediated survival
NF2 mutations appear in several sensitive lines, may impair mitotic checkpoint/cytokinesis
POLE mutations in sensitive lines may cause replication stress and mitotic vulnerability
